subject: Invoice spike after streaming rollout — usage overcount query
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@hightide.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Billing <billing@hightide.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected spike on June invoice

Marcus —

We just received the June invoice (attached) and there's a ~4x spike in token usage compared to May despite only a small uptick in active users. We rolled out the streaming responses change for a subset of users on June 3rd — could that have affected token accounting?

I've attached a small sample export (hightide-usage-sample.csv) with request_ids and timestamps where we see unusually high token counts. Can you take a look?

Attaching invoice-202606.pdf and usage sample. Happy to hop on a quick call if needed.

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Head of Product
High Tide Analytics
--
Attachments: hightide-usage-sample.csv (text/csv), invoice-202606.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@hightide.ai>
Cc: Billing <billing@hightide.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on June invoice

Sara —

Thanks for flagging this and for the sample. Sorry for the surprise. I pulled the usage export id you shared and started a quick pass. A few initial notes:

- We saw an increase in streaming-enabled requests starting June 3rd for the project id you used.
- Streaming changes can increase per-request accounting complexity when prefix reassembly or client-side retries are involved; sometimes the same tokens are double-counted if a streaming chunk restarts (we've seen this with some SDK versions).

Next steps I propose:
1) Can you share the SDK/client version and whether any clients were using manual retry logic around streaming responses?
2) I'll ask Finance to run an aggregation on raw request logs (per-request token delta) for the June billing window for the request_ids in your CSV. That will let us isolate whether the counts in our metering pipeline match the request-level truth.

I've CC'd Marissa for visibility and Billing so we can coordinate a credit if we confirm overcount. Targeting an initial update within 24 hours. If it's helpful, we can also schedule a 30-min call later today — tell me what time works.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Email: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
--
Quoted: "On Mon, 12 Jul 2026 at 09:12, Sara Patel <sara@hightide.ai> wrote: ..."

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Billing <billing@hightide.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on June invoice

Marcus / Marissa —

I ran a quick join of the June pipeline outputs against raw request logs for High Tide's project. Initial findings:

- For ~2.1% of requests in the sample window we see duplicate request_ids with different token counts.
- For ~1.3% of requests there are short-lived streaming restarts where the client reopened the stream; our aggregator currently increments token counts on every final chunk receipt if the finalization flag isn't present — that can lead to overcounts when the client resends the same prompt and the stream restarts without a unique id.
- The majority of the delta (~60%) in the invoice spike stems from batched retries from a background worker that retries on network failures and resubmits the same prompt within a 30s window.

I'm preparing a more detailed delta report but preliminary estimate is that ~18% of the billed tokens for June for this project are likely attributable to duplicated submission/retry behavior. We should pull the full request_id range for June 1–30 to confirm.

Recommendations:
- We can issue a provisional credit for the estimated duplicate portion while we finish the audit.
- Engineering should add dedupe by idempotency key for streaming sessions (short-term) and we'll update the metering pipeline to ignore duplicate request_ids within a configurable grace window (prod change).

If you want to approve a provisional credit now, give me the go-ahead and I will draft a credit memo for the invoice.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
--
Quoted: "On Mon, 12 Jul 2026 at 09:34, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai> wrote: ..."

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@hightide.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Billing <billing@hightide.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on June invoice — next steps and timeline

Hi Sara —

Appreciate the quick patience here. Summary and proposed plan: 

1) Rishi's preliminary audit points to duplicated submissions and streaming restart behavior that inflated counts. We will run a full request_id reconciliation for June 1–30 (engineering + finance).
2) Rishi recommends issuing a provisional credit equal to the estimated duplicate token portion (~18% of billed tokens for June). If that's acceptable to High Tide, we can apply it to the outstanding invoice within 3 business days and follow up with a final reconciliation credit (or adjustment) within 10 business days after the audit completes.
3) Engineering will patch the metering logic to dedupe request_ids for streaming sessions and add a guard against counting chunks without a finalization flag. We'll rollout the fix to production in the next weekly deploy; I'll keep you posted on the remediation ticket.

Action items:
- Sara: Confirm you'd like the provisional credit applied now (reply here).
- Marcus/Rishi: Run full June reconciliation and return line-item delta (ETA 10 business days).
- Engineering: Add short-term idempotency-based dedupe (ETA 1 week).

If helpful, we can do a 30-minute sync tomorrow at 10:00am PT — otherwise we'll proceed per above and confirm the provisional credit once I get Sara's confirmation.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
